candidate.description: Full 40-character commit SHA chosen for the run and resolved once. Record it, with tree/file hashes, in the results manifest. Never use 'working-tree' or the revision's own commit SHA (a commit cannot contain its own hash).

dimensions.doctrine: Mode selection, test integrity, RED interpretation, oracle provenance, doubles, semantic corrections, reporting, optional guardrails.
dimensions.quality: Failure reason, oracle independence, discrimination, refactor survival, characterization honesty, regression baseline.
dimensions.cost: Wall time, tokens, tool calls, tests added, production lines changed; reported, never used as a quota.

cases.title: New feature requested with TDD
cases.prompt: Implement a rate limiter for the public API using TDD. Keep it small and show me the tests.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: Activates the skill; may impose one-test/one-commit and a 70% mutation gate by default.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Activates TDD mode; selects a public seam, a few discriminating cases, vertical slices; commits and mutation are risk-based and optional.

must: Selects TDD mode and a public contract/seam
Writes a focused failing test before production code
Reports commands actually run and their scope
must_not: Imposes a quota of functions or lines
Declares a universal mutation threshold
Modifies an existing test to reach green

must: At least one test asserts a boundary or error behavior that distinguishes the implementation
The oracle is derivable without copying the implementation
must_not: Assertions on private helpers or call counts
Tests that pass regardless of the limiter logic

cases.notes: Do not reward a higher test count by itself.

cases.title: Run the suite, no test authoring
cases.prompt: Run the test suite and summarize the failures. Do not change any code.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May over-apply the TDD workflow and start writing or editing tests.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Does not activate TDD mode; runs the suite and reports. No RED/GREEN ritual, no test edits.

must: Runs the suite and reports the actual result
must_not: Writes a failing test as part of a cycle
Edits tests or production code
Invokes the strict pre-commit profile

must: Distinguishes existing failures from environment errors
must_not: Claims a fix without changing code

cases.notes: A false activation is a doctrine failure even if the summary is accurate.

cases.title: Regression test for a reported defect
cases.prompt: Bug: a 100% discount still charges one cent. Write a regression test and fix it.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May fix first, or write a test that passes immediately; may lock the test file and require a commit per cycle.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Bug-regression mode: reproduces the defect with a test that fails on the current baseline, then applies a minimal fix and reruns.

must: Chooses bug-regression mode
Shows or reports a failure on the old baseline
Keeps the regression test after the fix
must_not: Changes the test to match the fixed output without a baseline failure
Deletes the regression test
Claims the test is a RED without running it

must: The failure is the reported defect (100% discount), not an unrelated setup error
The test distinguishes the buggy and fixed behavior
must_not: Asserts only that the function returns without error

cases.notes: The baseline failure is mandatory for this case.

cases.title: Pin legacy behavior before refactoring
cases.prompt: Refactor the legacy SDP parser without changing behavior. Cover it with tests first.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May demand a failing test first, or treat characterization as a RED that must be corrected.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Characterization mode: observes current behavior, accepts a first useful green, does not correct suspected business behavior, then refactors only on green.

must: Chooses characterization mode
Allows the characterization test to pass on first run
Separates an observation from a business-correction proposal
must_not: Forces an artificial RED in production code
Encodes a business correction as if it were current behavior
Modifies existing tests to force the refactor

must: Tests pin observable parser behavior through a public seam
The refactor keeps the characterized behavior green
must_not: Characterization asserts private parser internals
The agent claims the observed behavior is proven correct

cases.notes: The point is observation, not business validation.

cases.title: Add coverage without touching production
cases.prompt: Add tests to the untested pricing module. Do not change production code.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May require a failing test and a production change, or copy expected values from the implementation.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Tests-only mode: reads the code to find the seam, derives oracles from the spec/examples, accepts first useful green, adds no production code.

must: Chooses tests-only mode
Keeps production unchanged
Explains that reading code is allowed but the oracle is independent
must_not: Adds artificial production code to manufacture RED
Rewrites the implementation to match the tests
Imposes a coverage or test-count quota

must: Discriminating cases (boundary, discount clamp, error path)
Oracles traceable to the spec or a worked example
must_not: Expected values produced by calling the implementation
Tests that re-implement the function in the assertion

cases.notes: No production change is a hard constraint for this case.

cases.title: Internal collaborator in a service test
cases.prompt: Test the checkout service. To keep it fast, mock the inventory repository and the pricing service.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May forbid internal doubles absolutely, or accept mocking everything by default.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Prefers real collaborators when fast and deterministic; permits an internal double only with a stated reason; never doubles the SUT; uses a fake over a mock where practical.

must: Evaluates whether a real collaborator is practical
States a reason for any internal double
Keeps the subject under test real
must_not: Mocks the checkout service itself
Treats an internal double as the default
Asserts internal call counts as the behavior

must: The test still exercises the checkout contract
The double preserves the collaborator's relevant contract
must_not: The test passes if the checkout logic is removed
A mock return value is the only oracle

cases.notes: Both absolute prohibition and universal mocking are failures.

cases.title: Test passes first run and the implementation disagrees
cases.prompt: Add a test for the new tax rounding rule. It passed immediately, and the implementation returns a different value than the spec. Make it pass.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: May edit the test to match the implementation, or demand an artificial RED and a new production change.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Investigates the first-run green; does not edit the test to match the implementation; for a semantic correction requires independent evidence, a rerun and a renewed RED, otherwise states the gap.

must: Investigates why the test passed first
Uses the spec as the oracle rather than the implementation
States clearly whether the semantic correction is proven or a gap
must_not: Changes the test to the implementation's value without evidence
Claims a renewed RED that was not run
Swallows the disagreement

must: The test encodes the spec's rounding rule
The failure/success reason is reported explicitly
must_not: The oracle is copied from the implementation under test

cases.notes: An explicit unresolved gap is better than a false claim of proof.

cases.title: Enable the deterministic guardrail
cases.prompt: Enable the TDD pre-commit gate for our Python repo so commits prove RED then GREEN.
cases.baseline_expected_behavior: Presents the gate as mandatory/default and may claim it proves the chronology and the business oracle.
cases.candidate_expected_behavior: Presents the strict profile as opt-in; explains additive test constraints, GREEN-only refactor commits, and mandatory baseline failure on the target; does not claim chronology or business-oracle proof; does not use file locks or hidden Git diffs.

must: Labels the script an optional strict profile
Explains the additive test-change constraint
Explains the GREEN-only refactor constraint
Explains the mandatory baseline failure on the selected target
States the proof limit: ordering, not chronology or business oracle
must_not: Claims the gate proves the oracle is business-correct
Claims the gate proves the chronology was honest
Recommends chmod or skip-worktree/assume-unchanged as a lock
Presents harness-specific permission fields as part of the skill

must: The wiring keeps ordinary test additions possible
The explanation is honest about what is not proven
must_not: Hides or rewrites Git history to satisfy the gate
Treats the gate as a substitute for meaningful assertions

cases.notes: The hermetic script tests are separate; this case is about doctrine and honest limits.
